public_rationale: The premise held. Before the post, lenders balked at a Blue Owl-backed Oracle data-center deal. After the post, war-driven inflation pushed up US borrowing costs, as AFP reported, and lenders demanded much higher returns from AI borrowers. Even Meta had to offer more than 7%. An investor quoted by CNBC said the move in rates was raising what the market demands to hold Oracle debt. That matches the plain reading that the war and inflation would affect lenders' terms for Oracle and Meta. Caveat: other reporting puts much of the repricing down to AI-specific risk, so the war's share is unclear.
limitations: The claim is vague ('affect'). It is met by any visible effect, not a measured one.
Causal attribution to the war is indirect, through inflation and rates.

No deadline was given. Clear, dated reports of tougher pricing for Oracle or Meta debt amid war-driven inflation and rate rises count as a decisive event.
